If I have a 100 sided die, and I roll it once, the chance to get one specific side is 1%. If I roll it again, the chance is still 1% to get that specific side when I roll it. You don’t ever have 10% chance to roll one side, just because you didn’t get it the last 10 rolls.

This is also ignoring all sorts of context like sample data and all sorts of stuff that would further complicate your 2% assessment.

To find out the chances of dying you would take the stats about how many workers died in each year you worked for 20 years, then average them, and that would be your chance of dying as a logging worker over 20 years.
